title: Derived reduction of an extension by a divisible sheaf
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with a final object, and let $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}$ and $R=(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], where $n\geq1$. Work in sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their cohomological derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $B,F$ be abelian sheaves such that $n:B\to B$ is an epimorphism and $n:F\to F$ is a monomorphism. Put $H=\ker(n:B\to B)$, with its natural $R$-module structure, and $\bar F=\operatorname{coker}(n:F\to F)$. Let $S$ be a short exact sequence $0\to B\to M\to F\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], with connecting morphism $\partial_S:F\to B[1]$, the last arrow of its derived short-exact-sequence triangle [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. For the derived change of rings $Lq=-\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}}R$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], there are natural identifications in $D(R)$
$$Lq(F)\simeq\bar F[0],\qquad Lq(B)\simeq H[1].$$
Normalize the second identification so that the scalar-extension unit $B\to\operatorname{Res}Lq(B)\simeq H[1]$ is the connecting morphism $\kappa_B$ of $0\to H\to B\xrightarrow{n}B\to0$. Thus $Lq(\partial_S)$ defines a canonical morphism $d_{S,n}:\bar F\to H[2]$ of $D(R)$. For every sheaf map $s:\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to F$, let $\bar s:R\to\bar F$ be its reduction. Under the derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], the morphism $d_{S,n}\bar s:R\to H[2]$ corresponds to
$$\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{s}F\xrightarrow{\partial_S}B[1]\xrightarrow{\kappa_B[1]}H[2]$$
in $D(\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C})$; in particular it is the Kummer-type connecting image of the extension boundary of $s$. These identifications and morphisms are natural for morphisms of short exact sequences satisfying these hypotheses and for exact inverse-image functors of geometric morphisms of topoi (left adjoints preserving finite limits), with the induced constant-ring identifications. Here $\operatorname{Res}$ is termwise restriction of scalars, and the adjunction has unit induced by $\mathbf Z_{\mathcal C}\to R$.

proof.text: Use derived adjunction compatibility and the unit-normalization lemma to fix $Lq\dashv\operatorname{Res}$, its K-flat unit formula, shift structure and coefficient isomorphism $e:Lq(Z)\simeq R$. The quotient-triangle lemma supplies residue kernel/cokernel structures and the ordinary-unit cokernel property, hence the scalar reduction presentation of $S$. Its multiplication triangle is computed on genuine $R$-complexes.

proof.text: Apply the single-cohomology normalization lemma to $F$ and $B$. Monicity on $F$ kills degree $-1$; epimorphy on $B$ kills degree zero. Its $R$-linear truncations give $\alpha_F,\alpha_B$, and $(-i[1])\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B=\delta_B$ fixes the Kummer sign. Their unit equations are exactly the normalized-identification record.

source.place: Paragraphs 4–5; live V2 proof obligations retained in the three extracted sublemmas and the landed normalization/exchange interfaces.

proof.text: Use the canonical short-exact-complex boundary $\partial_S$. It equals any boundary allowed in the statement: TR3 on the identity of the first two vertices gives $c:F\to F$ with $cg=g$ and $\partial_S=\delta'c$. Single-object full faithfulness and epimorphy of $g$ give $c=1$. Apply the same argument to the Kummer sequence. Define $d=\alpha_B[1]Lq(\partial_S)\alpha_F^{-1}$.

source.place: Paragraphs 4–5; live V2 proof obligations retained in the three extracted sublemmas and the landed normalization/exchange interfaces.

proof.text: The unit-normalization lemma gives $\bar s=\alpha_F Lq(s)e^{-1}$. Thus the adjunct of $d\bar s$ is $\operatorname{Res}(\alpha_B[1]Lq(\partial_Ss))\eta_Z$. Naturality of $\eta$, then its shift equation and $(\operatorname{Res}\alpha_B)\eta_B=\kappa_B$, turn this into $\kappa_B[1]\partial_Ss$. All single/restriction and $[1][1]=[2]$ comparisons are understood.

source.place: Paragraphs 4–5; live V2 proof obligations retained in the three extracted sublemmas and the landed normalization/exchange interfaces.

proof.text: For a map $f$ of extensions with induced $h:H\to H'$, $q:\bar F\to\bar F'$, compare adjuncts, which is injective on Hom by the scalar adjunction. For $\alpha_F$, naturality of $\eta$ and the quotient-unit equations reduce $\alpha'_FLq(f_3)=q\alpha_F$ to $p'f_3=\operatorname{Res}(q)p$, the quotient square. For $\alpha_B$, naturality of $\eta$ and the Kummer-unit equations reduce it to $\kappa'f_1=\operatorname{Res}(h[1])\kappa$, naturality of the canonical boundary for the map $(h,f_1,f_1)$ of Kummer sequences, with the single/restriction and shift comparisons. Naturality of $\partial_S$ then gives the $d$ square. No map is assumed invertible.

source.place: Paragraphs 4–5; live V2 proof obligations retained in the three extracted sublemmas and the landed normalization/exchange interfaces.

proof.text: For exact geometric inverse image, restriction commutes through the induced coefficient identifications. The unit-normalization lemma supplies shift-compatible derived adjunctions whose units on K-flat complexes are the termwise units; the quotient-triangle lemma supplies fully faithful restriction and the ordinary-unit cokernel property. Flat-term K-flat resolutions exist and have termwise monic $n$, so the derived cokernel adjoint exchange theorem applies and gives the shift-compatible, mate-unit-normalized isomorphism. Exactness identifies the pulled-back quotient and Kummer presentations. Apply normalized scalar boundary naturality to these presentation isomorphisms: it gives both $\alpha$ squares and exactly the degree-two boundary square.
